clue.text: Scotsman's cry of surprise tucking into cheese roll

indicators.note: one piece tucks itself into another, so the exclamation goes inside the cheese

parts.note: brie is a soft French cheese
och is a Scottish exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A Scot exclaims in surprise while biting into a cheese roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A brioche is a sweet, rich French bread roll.

clue.text: Formula fully developed outside the City

indicators.note: the ripe word goes round the outside of the City's postcode letters

parts.note: fruit fully developed is ripe
EC is the postcode area of the City of London

explanation.surface: A formula is perfected beyond the boundaries of London's financial district.
explanation.definitionFit: A recipe is a set formula of ingredients and instructions for a dish.

clue.text: Game fellow one's seen crossing a road

parts.note: Bill is a man's name, so a fellow

indicators.note: the letters for one's lie across, on either side of, the a-plus-road piece

parts.note: one is I, so one's is IS

explanation.surface: A man is spotted walking across a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Billiards is a cue game played on a cloth-covered table.

clue.text: Wrong direction taken by friends on the Continent

parts.note: amis is French for friends
S, south, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: Some European friends have headed off the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiss means faulty or out of order, so wrong.

clue.text: University cricket club with yen to introduce a Mexican plant

indicators.note: the yen letter goes in front, introducing what follows

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: A college cricket club brings in Japanese money to import an exotic plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The yucca is a spiky-leaved plant native to Mexico and the American south-west.

clue.text: Mostly courteous hanger-on with old Communist committee

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: courteous means polite
a bur is a clinging seed head, so a hanger-on

explanation.surface: A rather polite clinger joins forces with an elderly figure.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of a Communist party, notably the Soviet one.

clue.text: Novel her aunt and daughter disentangle

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A novel tells how a woman's aunt and daughter sort out a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but it is the anagram signal: HERAUNT rearranges to UNTHREA.
explanation.definitionFit: To unthread is to pull out the thread, hence to untangle or unravel.

clue.text: Mistakes made by English regiment locking up deserter

indicators.note: the regiment letters enclose the deserter as if jailing him

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment
a rat is one who deserts a cause

explanation.surface: An English regiment jails a soldier who went absent, a series of blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are listed printing errors, the plural of erratum.

clue.text: Supply latest info on appearing for trial by court?

parts.note: someone up before the magistrate is appearing in court
to court someone is to woo or date them

explanation.surface: A reporter brings news of someone due before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is the romantic verb, to date.
explanation.definitionFit: To update someone is to give them the most recent information.

clue.text: Head of George Rex executed in army base?

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following name is used
executed means beheaded here, so the first letter goes

parts.note: Rex Harrison was the English actor of My Fair Lady fame

explanation.surface: A king's head is cut off at a military post.
explanation.walkthrough: Rex is not a king but the actor Rex Harrison; beheading his surname leaves ARRISON.
explanation.definitionFit: A garrison is a body of troops stationed at a fort, or the fort itself.

clue.text: Stone in fancy ring men found in river

indicators.note: the following pieces are found inside the river's name

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: fancy here means elaborated, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: A decorative ring set with a gem turns up in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairngorm is a smoky-brown quartz gemstone named after the Scottish mountains.

clue.text: Item knocked down by male serf

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
an auction item knocked down by the hammer is a lot

explanation.surface: A man sells a lot at auction to a peasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a Spartan serf, and by extension any slave or serf.

clue.text: Resin from tree I observed around East

indicators.note: the tree and I go around the letter for East

parts.note: the elm is a tree
E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: I watched a tree yielding resin somewhere in the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Elemi is a fragrant resin from tropical trees used in varnishes and ointments.

clue.text: What act as channels for processing sago, I hope!

indicators.note: food processing breaks things down, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone hopes their gullet copes with a sago pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: The oesophagi, plural of oesophagus, are the tubes carrying food to the stomach.

clue.text: Extension built by woman concealing surname, do we hear?

indicators.note: the woman's name holds the second piece hidden inside

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

indicators.note: the letter for the surname is said aloud and written as it sounds

parts.note: X is the mark used for an unknown name, such as Malcolm X's

explanation.surface: A woman hides her family name while building an extension.
explanation.walkthrough: An X marks a name kept unknown, as with Malcolm X; spoken, the letter sounds like the two-letter word that the woman's name then wraps.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an extension.

clue.text: Showing impatience on road in area south of Wandsworth

definitions.meaning: an impatient driver keeps sounding the car horn
A district of south London below Wandsworth

explanation.definitionFit: Tooting is both honking a horn and a south London district in the borough of Wandsworth.

clue.text: Everything's OK if you're Cratchit's nephew!

definitions.meaning: a British catchphrase meaning there you are, all done
Bob Cratchit of A Christmas Carol would be uncle to his nephew

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means everything is settled, and literally names Bob as uncle.

clue.text: Dicky in charge of appeal? That's not allowed

parts.note: dicky is British slang for unwell or shaky
it means sex appeal

explanation.surface: A sickly person in charge makes an appeal that gets refused.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicit means forbidden by law or custom, so not permitted.

clue.text: Tea taken outside in porcelain vessels?

indicators.note: the tea word goes outside, around the other piece

parts.note: cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Tea is carried outdoors in fine cups.
explanation.definitionFit: China is porcelain, and by extension the crockery made of it.

clue.text: Continental painter housed by a Scotsman, perhaps

indicators.note: the painter sits inside the Scotsman's name as if lodging there

parts.note: Euan is a typically Scottish man's name
a painter is a rope tying a boat to its mooring

explanation.surface: An artist from the Continent lodges with a man from Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painter' is the nautical rope, not an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Continental in British usage means from mainland Europe.

clue.text: Swish old philosopher referred to in speech

indicators.note: something spoken rather than written signals a sound-alike

parts.note: Bertrand Russell was a British philosopher of the last century

explanation.surface: A dated thinker is mentioned with a swish in a lecture.
explanation.definitionFit: A swish is a soft rustling sound, as of silk.

clue.text: Conservative party host upset about gossip

parts.note: the Mad Hatter hosts the tea party in Alice in Wonderland

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned over, so the letters read upward

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A Tory hosting a party is upset about tittle-tattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip is someone who chatters idly about others.

clue.text: Starchy union leader at city plant

parts.note: starchy means stiff and prim

indicators.note: a leader is the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A stiff union boss is posted to a city factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like an industrial site; it is the flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Primula is the genus of flowering plants including primroses.

clue.text: Be ruthless — rotten to past love!

indicators.note: rotten means decayed, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: love is zero, or nothing, in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone treats a former lover cruelly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop at nothing is to be prepared to do anything, however ruthless.

clue.text: Able to remember plunderer endlessly pinching wine

indicators.note: pinching means grasping, so one piece holds the other
the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a reiver is a Border raider or plunderer
tent is a deep red Spanish wine

explanation.surface: A raider steals wine and remembers where he got it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts REIVER to REIVE, which then holds TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retentive memory is one that holds on to facts well.

clue.text: Monkey in trading centre eating some bananas

indicators.note: the market word takes in the other piece as if eating

parts.note: a mart is a market

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A monkey in a market helps itself to a few bananas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but is the anagram signal, turning SOME into MOSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a small South American monkey.

clue.text: Sort of cinema way up by this writer's home

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: RD, road, is a way
this writer is I, so this writer has is I'VE
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone drives up the road to their own house.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive-in cinema lets audiences watch films from their parked cars.

clue.text: School head set up current ruddy course programmes!

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter
in a down clue set up means read upward

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
ruddy and bally are mild British euphemisms for bloody

explanation.surface: A headteacher sets up the blasted timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns I BALLY round to YLLABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Syllabi, the plural of syllabus, are outlines of courses of study.

clue.text: North American animal shelter taking in pony regularly

indicators.note: the shelter takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for birds or animals

indicators.note: every other letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A shed is giving refuge to a pony.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a wild dog of North and Central America.

clue.text: One wallows in mud with it on Italian river

parts.note: with it means fashionable, so hip
the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: A trendy creature rolls in the mud by an Italian river.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippopotamus is famous for wallowing in mud and water.
